original_poem:
கூட்டம் கடந்து வருவன காணின்  
வீட்டம் எனவொன்றோ விளைந்ததே நெஞ்சே  
காட்டின் கழுமல் தழீஇயக் கண்ணின்  
நாடன் வருவான் எனக் கண்டதே நெஞ்சே
translated_poem:
As the crowds pass by,  
Is there something called home, O heart?  
At the sight of a flower in the forest,  
Did you think the lover would come, O heart?

stanzas.loss_note: காட்டின் கழுமல் தழீஇயக் கண்ணின் refers to a forest flower seen in passing — in Sangam akam convention this is a tinai-specific nature image (likely mullai or palai) that triggers involuntary hope of the lover's return; 'a flower in the forest' loses the precise emotional-ecological coding of the original.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: a glimpsed forest flower as involuntary trigger of the lover's imagined return
the heart's desolate questioning of whether home or union is even possible

cultural_entities.translation_note: The Sangam convention of addressing the heart (nenjē) as a separate interlocutor — a defining akam rhetorical device — is partially preserved as 'O heart' but its structural role as the poem's internal witness is not conveyed.
